env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# A ?? whose fallback is an interpolated string, lowered inside a call
# the MustNonNil wrapper covers, must nest inside the wrapper in eject
# instead of dropping the interpolation. The wrapped call stores a Go
# package's pointer result into a declared non-nil location; the option
# and interpolation lowerings run after the wrapper, so the fallback
# replacement ends where the ?? tail insert sits. The plain fallback
# is the control that already nested.

cd m
logos run .
stdout '^reader fallback 7$'
stdout '^reader plain$'
cp stdout $WORK/native-stdout.txt

logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native-stdout.txt
go vet ./...
exec $GOROOT/bin/gofmt -l .
! stdout .
cd ..
cd ..

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/wrapdefault

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

func maybeName(n int) string? {
	if n == 7 {
		return "seven"
	}
	return nil
}

func showReader(r *strings.Reader) {
	var sb strings.Builder
	if _, err := r.WriteTo(&sb); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("error", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Println(sb.String())
}

func readerOrInterp(name string?, tag int) *strings.Reader {
	return strings.NewReader(name ?? $"reader fallback {tag}")
}

func readerOrPlain(name string?) *strings.Reader {
	return strings.NewReader(name ?? "reader plain")
}

func main() {
	showReader(readerOrInterp(nil, 7))
	showReader(readerOrPlain(nil))
}
